13	- When a measurement contradicts something in the doc, correct the doc **in the same session** and state which of its recorded candidate causes were confirmed versus eliminated — the doc is read as authoritative by the next session, including by me.
14	- Debug-rig direction as agreed 2026-10-03, in this order: (1) grow the existing bridge into the debugger — block-column and entity-in-box probes, agent relocate, failure reasons carried on the event; (2) a dev-only "keep ticking while the client is paused" switch behind `run/config/mcbuddy.properties`, default off; (3) a window-off-screen script instead of minimizing, since a minimized window hard-stalls the integrated server and the game rewrites `run/options.txt` on exit so vsync/fps tuning there does not survive.
15	- Deliberately rejected: a headless dedicated-server test rig. The fake-player path is client-side (`@Environment(CLIENT)` accessors, the embedded `Connection`, the `tickConnection` mixin), so that rig would validate code we do not ship.
16	- Deferred with a stated trigger: a superflat fixture world, only *after* walks pass on natural terrain — switching earlier would hide the spawn-geometry class of bug that has twice produced a false "it works". He OK'd the resulting permanent block edits to the scratch save.
17	- **M3 design he ratified on 2026-10-03** (full line-level evidence lives in `docs/HANDOFF.md`; do not re-litigate, extend): break and place go only through synthesized inbound packets whose handlers already run vanilla's own gauntlet — never `ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` (post-verdict, skips every check), never `setBlock`/`/setblock`/`/fill` command dispatch. Permissions tier by *does it bypass player identity*, not by perceived danger, and direct writes are constrained structurally (must broadcast, must be inside loaded chunks) rather than by a toggle that can be flipped. Creative stays for M3 because the M2 gait depends on `isCreative` and creative insta-mines; real survival mining is its own milestone gated on local physics prediction. The stand-position solver reuses vanilla's reach predicate instead of a new formula.
18	**Orchestration is PTC, not a step DSL (ratified 2026-10-04).** The earlier `agent.run {steps:[...]}` draft is superseded: he chose *programmatic tool calling* — the model writes a small program with real `for`/`if`/`await`, a host executes it, and only the program's return value re-enters context. So do not re-propose a bespoke plan vocabulary; it is a worse re-invention of the language. Orchestration lives in TypeScript outside the game process; tick-level decisions (deadlines, retries, the pathfinder no-go set) stay in Java because `status` must still answer truthfully what the agent is doing.

20	**Product target he stated 2026-10-04:** "挂一个agent在后台跟我玩那种类型" — a companion playing alongside him while he does something else. Consequences to design for, in order: events push rather than poll; `agent.say` needs its own rate limit before it can run unattended (it bypasses vanilla's `detectChatRateSpam`, since a fake player cannot sign chat); the host is long-lived (an MCP server the client owns), which is precisely why moving the runner in-process is *not* needed yet.
21	
22	**The dev world is not a constant.** Random ticks let mangrove vines grow into cells `world.pad` had cleared, which silently voided an A/B run made ~1.5h after its baseline (two walks wedged on ground that had been clean). Re-prepare the fixture immediately before measuring; treat cross-session comparisons as void.
23	
24	**M4 (the MCP shell) — spec checked, shell shipped, registered 2026-10-04.** The old gate ("do not write the handshake from memory; the claim that the 2026-07-28 revision retired `initialize`/`Mcp-Session-Id` is unverified") is **resolved and the claim was correct**: verified verbatim from the spec changelog (SEP-2567 removed protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header; SEP-2575 made MCP stateless by removing the `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake, with each request carrying its version in `_meta`). Results carry `resultType` (`complete`/`input_required`), and only four `_meta` keys are reserved. Unresolved in the spec pages I read: whether JSON-RPC batching is still allowed, what a server must do with an unknown version, and the notification method list — treat those as **not** confirmed. `scripts/mcp.mjs` (zero deps, stdio, 6 tools: status/events/look/column/find/run_program) is self-tested against the live game as a spawned subprocess, all round trips < 130 ms; write operations are reachable **only** through `run_program`, so don't add per-write tools. The PTC surface now lives in `scripts/ptc-host.mjs` shared by the CLI and the shell — one definition of the tools, never two. He OK'd registering it (local scope: `D:\mcbuddy-mod\.qoder\settings.local.json`, **not** gitignored in this repo, so never `git add .`), and OK'd answering `initialize` as a measurement of which revision the host client declares — read `mcp.log`'s `client_protocol=` after `/mcp reload` before deciding whether that branch stays.
25	
26	**Listening constraint for the background companion.** Chat arrives in the event queue as `{from, text}`, but `!buddy ...` lines are cancelled at `handleChat`'s HEAD and consumed as commands, so they never reach the event stream. A companion that reacts to his voice therefore sees ordinary chat only, and any command surface has to be read from the command side, not the event side. Bidirectional chat (hear him, reply via `agent.say`) was proven working end to end on 2026-10-04 with no engine change — the inbound wiring already existed from M0.5.

312	### 协议事实是查证的，不是回忆的
313	
314	DESIGN/HANDOFF 里"2026-07-28 退役了 `initialize`/`Mcp-Session-Id`"原本是一条**未核实断言**。现在核实了，逐字引 spec changelog：
315	
316	- `Remove protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the Streamable HTTP transport.`（SEP-2567）
317	- `Make MCP stateless: remove the `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake.`
318	- `Every request now carries its protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`).`
319	- `Clients SHOULD identify themselves on each request (`io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`), and servers SHOULD identify themselves in each result's `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`).`（SEP-2575）
320	- `_meta` 里被保留的键只有四个：`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` / `clientInfo` / `clientCapabilities` / `logLevel`。
321	- `A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params).`
322	- stdio 帧格式：`newline-delimited JSON-RPC over a byte stream`，且 `Mcp-Session-Id` 之类的 HTTP 头**与 stdio 无关**。
323	- 结果里有 `resultType`，取值 `complete`（成功）或 `input_required`（还要输入）。`tools/call` 结果字段是 `resultType` / `content` / `structuredContent` / `isError`，并且**给了 structuredContent 就必须同时给一个序列化好的 text block**（旧客户端兼容）。
324	
325	**仍未查到的**（别当成已确认）：JSON-RPC batch 数组是否还允许、spec 对"未知 protocolVersion"要求服务端怎么处理、notification 方法名单。这三条我读到的页面没有明确写。

328	
329	- `scripts/mcp.mjs`：**零依赖**（不 npm install，供应链就是这么省的）stdio JSON-RPC 外壳，把桥接的读能力 + PTC 宿主暴露成 6 个工具：`mcbuddy_status` `mcbuddy_events` `mcbuddy_look` `mcbuddy_column` `mcbuddy_find` `mcbuddy_run_program`。
330	- **改世界的一律走 `run_program`**，不给 `agent.dig` 单独发工具位：工具少而粗是预算，而控制流本来就该写在程序里。
331	- `scripts/ptc.mjs` 拆成 `ptc-host.mjs`（`ask` / `mcbuddy` / `runProgram`）+ 一个瘦 CLI。拆的**唯一理由**：外壳和 CLI 必须共用同一份工具定义，否则协议和调试台会对"`mcbuddy.dig` 是什么"产生分歧——那正是决策里"避免同一逻辑维护两遍"要避免的事。

#### Thinking

93	export async function runProgram(source, { onLog = () => {}, timeoutMs = PLAN_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {
94	  // A plan may be written as `export default async (m) => ...` for the editor's sake; the vm has no
95	  // module system, so the wrapper is stripped and the expression is what runs. Not anchored, because
96	  // a plan normally opens with comments explaining itself.
97	  const body = source.replace(/export\s+default\s+/, '').trim();
98	  const context = vm.createContext({ mcbuddy, log: onLog });
99	  const startedAt = Date.now();
100	  let timer;
101	  try {
102	    const factory = await vm.runInContext(`(${body})`, context, { timeout: timeoutMs });
103	    // The timer must be cleared, not just raced against: an uncancelled 180s handle keeps the event
104	    // loop alive after the answer is already printed, so a caller waiting on this process hangs for
105	    // the full deadline after every successful run.
106	    const result = await Promise.race([
107	      factory(mcbuddy),
108	      new Promise((_, reject) => {
109	        timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('plan deadline exceeded')), timeoutMs);
110	      }),
111	    ]);
112	    return { ok: true, ms: Date.now() - startedAt, result };
113	  } catch (err) {
114	    return { ok: false, ms: Date.now() - startedAt, error: String(err?.message ?? err) };
115	  } finally {
116	    clearTimeout(timer);
117	  }

**M4 闭环之后立刻暴露的两个洞（已修一个，实测在下面）**：产品目标是"挂在后台陪我玩"，而 PTC 程序当时**读不到事件、也不会等**：
- `vm.createContext({ mcbuddy, log })` 是个全新的 context，**没有 Node 的全局**：`setTimeout is not defined` 是实测（`Date`/`Math`/`Promise` 这些 intrinsic 在，`console`/`setTimeout` 不在，所以 `log` 早就是必需的而不是风格）。
- `mcbuddy` 对象里**没有 `events`**，而 `mcp.mjs:156` 的 `mcbuddy_events` 工具用的是同一个 `ask('events.poll')`。同一个能力在工具面有、在 PTC 面没有，程序就只能把事件读进模型上下文 —— 正好是选 PTC 想省掉的那笔预算。
- 修法（`scripts/ptc-host.mjs`）：`mcbuddy.events = cursor => ask('events.poll', {cursor: cursor ?? 0})`，并把宿主的 `sleep` 放进 context。放 `sleep` 时**故意不 unref**：unref 之后 CLI 会在 plan 还在 await 它的时候直接退出，答案一个字都不打。
- 实测（`scratch/ptc-events.mjs` 走 CLI，新进程）：`{events_shape:{cursor:0,n:0}, sleep_worked:true, wall_ms:2050, tick_delta:42, tps:"20.49"}`，进程 `real 2.238s` 退出（说明上一个 `clearTimeout` 修复没被这次改动弄回去）。
- **事件环当时是空的**（`events:[]`、`status.event_cursor:0`），所以 `m.events` 只证明了"调用通了、形状对"，**没有证明带载荷的事件能从 PTC 面读出来**。要证它得先制造一条事件（走一步 / 让人类说一句话），下次做别再当成已确认。
- **改 `scripts/*.mjs` 不会立刻生效到 agent 面**：外壳是 App 起的长驻进程，同一段程序经 `mcp_call` 仍然 `m.events is not a function`（`ms:0`），经 CLI 就成功。所以**改完外壳要重启那条 server（面板里 disable/enable，或新会话）才算数**。
```

feat: let a plan wait and listen, because a companion that can only be told is not a companion

M4 closed from the other side: a new session's tool surface really has the 6
mcbuddy_* tools, and mcp_call mcbuddy_status answered tick=55150 with
others[0]={Player814, dist:6.4}. run_program returned in 38ms, so the
shell -> PTC host -> bridge -> live agent chain is proven from the agent side,
not just from a self-test that spawns its own shell.

Two measurements taken while doing it:
- probe.mjs status twice with 15s between: tick 58933 -> 59236 over 15152ms
  = 20.00 tps while client_paused:true. keep_ticking_while_paused holds the
  nominal rate, it does not merely let a few ticks through.
- mcp.log tail: after initialize{2025-11-25} every request arrives with
  client_protocol=unstated. The per-request _meta branch is unreachable for
  this client; the negotiated version is fixed per connection.

Then the PTC surface was missing exactly what the background companion needs:
- vm.createContext gives a plan no Node globals, so `setTimeout is not defined`
  (measured) — a program could not pace itself. `log` was load-bearing all
  along, not stylistic.
- mcbuddy had no `events` while mcp.mjs:156 exposes the same ask('events.poll')
  as mcbuddy_events, so reacting to anything meant pulling events into model
  context — the budget PTC was chosen to save.

sleep is passed in un-ref'd deliberately: unref lets the CLI exit while a plan
is still awaiting it and print nothing.

CLI-verified (fresh process, same live bridge): {events_shape:{cursor:0,n:0},
sleep_worked:true, wall_ms:2050, tick_delta:42, tps:"20.49"}, exits in 2.24s
so the earlier clearTimeout fix survived. Not yet proven: the ring was empty,
so no event with a payload has been read through the PTC surface. And the
App's shell is long-lived — the same program through mcp_call still says
m.events is not a function until that server is restarted.
```

Permissions tier by *does it bypass player identity*, not by perceived danger, and direct writes are constrained structurally (must broadcast, must be inside loaded chunks) rather than by a toggle that can be flipped. Creative stays for M3 because the M2 gait depends on `isCreative` and creative insta-mines; real survival mining is its own milestone gated on local physics prediction. Orchestration lives in TypeScript outside the game process; tick-level decisions (deadlines, retries, the pathfinder no-go set) stay in Java because `status` must still answer truthfully what the agent is doing.

26	**Listening constraint for the background companion.** Chat arrives in the event queue as `{from, text}`, but `!buddy ...` lines are cancelled at `handleChat`'s HEAD and consumed as commands, so they never reach the event stream. A companion that reacts to his voice therefore sees ordinary chat only, and any command surface has to be read from the command side, not the event side. 308	Modrinth 上"会挖矿的 AI companion"（Core Companion、Nova MC Companion、CraftyAI 等）全部是**驱动真实客户端输入**（多数靠 Baritone），没有一个把"经原版裁决的方块交互"做成协议。我们的差异点是 agent 本身就是玩家、且**没有客户端可模拟**，所以这条链路不是重复建设。

310	## M4：MCP stdio 外壳（2026-10-04 已实现并实测）
311	
312	### 协议事实是查证的，不是回忆的
313	
314	DESIGN/HANDOFF 里"2026-07-28 退役了 `initialize`/`Mcp-Session-Id`"原本是一条**未核实断言**。现在核实了，逐字引 spec changelog：
315	
316	- `Remove protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the Streamable HTTP transport.`（SEP-2567）
317	- `Make MCP stateless: remove the `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake.`
318	- `Every request now carries its protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`).`
319	- `Clients SHOULD identify themselves on each request (`io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`), and servers SHOULD identify themselves in each result's `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`).`（SEP-2575）
320	- `_meta` 里被保留的键只有四个：`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` / `clientInfo` / `clientCapabilities` / `logLevel`。
321	- `A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params).`
322	- stdio 帧格式：`newline-delimited JSON-RPC over a byte stream`，且 `Mcp-Session-Id` 之类的 HTTP 头**与 stdio 无关**。
323	- 结果里有 `resultType`，取值 `complete`（成功）或 `input_required`（还要输入）。`tools/call` 结果字段是 `resultType` / `content` / `structuredContent` / `isError`，并且**给了 structuredContent 就必须同时给一个序列化好的 text block**（旧客户端兼容）。
324	
325	**仍未查到的**（别当成已确认）：JSON-RPC batch 数组是否还允许、spec 对"未知 protocolVersion"要求服务端怎么处理、notification 方法名单。这三条我读到的页面没有明确写。
326	
327	### 实现
328	
329	- `scripts/mcp.mjs`：**零依赖**（不 npm install，供应链就是这么省的）stdio JSON-RPC 外壳，把桥接的读能力 + PTC 宿主暴露成 6 个工具：`mcbuddy_status` `mcbuddy_events` `mcbuddy_look` `mcbuddy_column` `mcbuddy_find` `mcbuddy_run_program`。
330	- **改世界的一律走 `run_program`**，不给 `agent.dig` 单独发工具位：工具少而粗是预算，而控制流本来就该写在程序里。
331	- `scripts/ptc.mjs` 拆成 `ptc-host.mjs`（`ask` / `mcbuddy` / `runProgram`）+ 一个瘦 CLI。拆的**唯一理由**：外壳和 CLI 必须共用同一份工具定义，否则协议和调试台会对"`mcbuddy.dig` 是什么"产生分歧——那正是决策里"避免同一逻辑维护两遍"要避免的事。
332	- 我们**回答 `initialize`** —— 这条原本是"等测量再决定"，现在测到了：App 客户端就是握手版的 `2025-11-25`，所以 `initialize` 不是历史包袱，是**必需**的。同时保留无握手路径（`_meta` 里带版本的 2026-07-28 形态），两条都要对，因为结果字段按协商到的版本发。
333	- 工具执行失败 = `isError: true` 的**协议成功**，不是 JSON-RPC error。原因是模型需要拿到的载荷，包成 transport error 会被客户端的样板话盖掉。
334	
335	### 实测（12:20 起客户端，`scratch/mcpselftest.mjs` 自己 spawn 外壳、写 stdin、读 stdout）
336	
337	- 往返时间：`initialize` 71ms、`tools/list` 71ms、`mcbuddy_status` 127ms、`mcbuddy_column` 127ms —— 全部 < 130ms，而且并发正确（id 4 的回话排在 id 3 前面）。
338	- `tools/list` 广告到的名字就是那 6 个。
339	- **`run_program` 经外壳跑通闭环**：`ms: 51`，返回值只有程序自己那份 `{tick:10826, me:{-170.5,86,81.5}, human:{name:"Player814", dist:6.4}}`，`resultType:"complete"`，`_meta` 带 `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`。也就是说"外壳 → PTC 宿主 → 桥接 → 活的 agent"这条链已经通。
340	- 错误路径也实测：未知方法 → `-32601`；`run_program` 传空 source → `-32602`（spec 规定的码）。
341	
342	### 修掉的一个真 bug（M4 逼出来的）
343	
344	`runProgram` 用 `Promise.race` 卡 deadline，但那个 `setTimeout` **从来没被 clear**：plan 147ms 就把答案打出来了，进程却还要活满 180s 才退出——因为未取消的 handle 吊着事件循环。CLI 时代这只是烦人（看着像卡死）；外壳里 `run_program` 是同一个进程内调用，客户端会直接等到超时。现在 `finally { clearTimeout(timer) }`，实测 `time node scripts/ptc.mjs scratch/tp.mjs` = **0.21s**（135ms 的 plan）。
345	
346	### M4 的下一步（差一次客户端接入）
347	
348	1. **注册目标选错了文件，别再重犯**：我写的是 `D:\mcbuddy-mod\.qoder\settings.local.json` —— 那是 **qodercli 的 local 作用域**，而用户用的是 **Electron 桌面端**（`%APPDATA%\com.qoder.app.stable`），它不读这个文件，也**没有 `/mcp reload` 这种斜杠命令**。全盘搜过：App 目录下没有任何含 `mcpServers` 的 json，当前活着的 `browser-use` / `node-repl` / `extension-market` 都是内置或插件带的，不落盘成用户可编辑的 MCP 配置。**所以 App 端接入只能走它自己的 MCP 设置界面**，填 `command: node` + `args: ["D:/mcbuddy-mod/scripts/mcp.mjs"]`（绝对路径 —— 子进程的 cwd 不在仓库）。那份 settings.local.json 对 CLI 仍然有用，对 App 无害，留着。另注：本仓库 `.gitignore` **没有**忽略 `.qoder/`，它是 untracked，别顺手 `git add .`。
349	2. **客户端版本已经量到了，别再猜**：App 真的 spawn 了外壳（`mcp.log` 里两轮 `listening`），顺序是 **先 `server/discover`、再 `initialize{protocolVersion:'2025-11-25'}`**。第一次连不上（`MCP_RUNTIME_UNKNOWN`，App 侧 `durationMs 223/202`）的根因是**我**：白名单里没有 `2025-11-25`，于是回了自家 `2026-07-28`，而"回一个客户端没要求的版本"按协议就是让它断开 —— `initialize` 之后它一个请求都没再发，和这个解释完全吻合。现在外壳做的是**真协商**：能服务的版本就照收（`SUPPORTED` 里含 2025-11-25），不能才回自家最新；`resultType` 只在 `2026-07-28` 发、`structuredContent` 从 `2025-06-18` 起发。实测两种形态：`initialize{2025-11-25}` → 回 `2025-11-25`、`tools/list` 6 个、`tools/call` 结果键 `{_meta,content,isError,structuredContent}`（无 resultType）、`others[0].name` 读到人；无握手 + `_meta{2026-07-28}` → 结果带 `resultType`，`run_program` 7ms 返回 tick。
350	   **`server/discover` 仍未解决**：不是 spec 里的方法，我们回 `-32601`，而客户端**继续发了 initialize**，所以它不是致命的。外壳现在把每个请求的 `params` 也记进 `mcp.log`（客户端拥有子进程 stderr，不记就读不到），下次重试若还失败，先看那行 `method=server/discover params=...`。
351	
352	**接通了（13:0x，用户界面能看到 6 个工具）**，外壳日志实测的顺序：
353	
354	```
355	method=server/discover  _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion=2026-07-28
356	                        clientInfo={"name":"qoder-desktop-mcp-host","version":"1.0.0"}
357	                        clientCapabilities.extensions: io.modelcontextprotocol/ui(mimeTypes:["text/html;profile=mcp-app"]),
358	                        com.qoder/auth-state-v1, com.qoder/request-context-v1,
359	                        com.qoder/search-telemetry-v1, com.qoder/knowledge-telemetry-v1
360	method=initialize       protocolVersion=2025-11-25
361	negotiated 2025-11-25 with qoder-desktop-mcp-host
362	method=notifications/initialized
363	method=tools/list  (两次)
364	```
365	
366	三条值得记住：
367	
368	- "我的客户端是哪一版"不是一个值而是两个：**发现阶段按 `2026-07-28` 报自己，会话阶段落到 `initialize{2025-11-25}`**。外壳按 initialize 的结果决定字段形态，实测正确。
369	- 它声明了 `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`（`text/html;profile=mcp-app`）—— **这个客户端能渲染 mcp-app**。以后要"实时看 agent 在哪 / 眼前是什么"，正解是给一个 UI 资源，而不是发截图（发截图是禁的）。
370	- `server/discover` 我们仍回 `-32601`，客户端照旧继续握手，所以它不是致命路径。真要支持得先见到它的成功响应 schema，别猜。
371	
372	**但 agent 侧还没拿到**：App 运行时已经连上（有握手、有 tools/list、界面列出 6 个工具），而我自己会话的 MCP 工具面（`mcp_list` 全量 95 条）里**没有任何 `mcbuddy_*`**。差的只是"把这个 server 注入 agent 工具面"这一步 —— 大概率要新开会话，或面板上那条 server 还有一个"启用/连接到会话"的开关。**闭环的终点是从新会话里 `mcp_call` 一次 `mcbuddy_status`。**
373	3. **长计划超过客户端 timeout**：v1 是阻塞式（`MCBUDDY_PLAN_TIMEOUT` 默认 180s）。真撞上了再决定是"分段调 + 靠 `mcbuddy_events` 续"还是 spec 里的 tasks/`input_required`，现在猜没有意义。
374	
375	## 看得见人类：`status.others`（2026-10-04 已实测）
376	
377	后台 companion 的第一块前置：回答"人在哪"。`BuddyAgent.otherPlayersJson()` 遍历 `getPlayerList().getPlayers()` 排除自己，给 `{name,x,y,z,dist}`（坐标取整到 0.1），挂在 `status` 结果的 `others` 字段上。
378	
379	实测（同一份存档，人类是 Player814）：`"others": [{"name":"Player814","x":-171.7,"y":86,"z":87.8,"dist":5.2}]` —— 一个真实玩家、一条记录，`dist` 与两处坐标的手算一致。桥接侧只改了 `BridgeHandlers` 的 `status` 分支，`agent.teleport` 那条 rig 操作也顺带在同一个 plan 里实测了（`{"from":"-172.5,86.0,82.5","moved":true,"to":"-170.5,86.0,81.5","adjusted":true}`，`adjusted:true` 是它自己找可站点）。
380	
381	**别误读日志**：02:36 那次 `runclient.log` 里连着两次 `pick`（stone 再 dirt）**不是桥接或 `world.find` 坏了**，是当时 `scratch/hut.mjs` 里写的 `!picked.held.startsWith('')` 恒为 false（任何字符串都以 `''` 开头），导致材料循环永不 break、把四种候选全试了一遍。scratch 不进版本库，但"判空用 `held.length > 0`，别用 `startsWith('')`"值得留一句。
382

44	// Awaitable walk: submit, then follow the event stream until that task reports. Polling the cursor
45	// rather than the position means a step cannot look idle just because the tick rate dipped.
46	export async function walkTo(cell) {

49	  if (!accepted.accepted) return { status: 'rejected', reason: accepted.reason };
50	  const deadline = Date.now() + Math.max(30000, accepted.est_ticks_lower_bound * 3 * 50);
51	  for (;;) {
52	    await sleep(700);
53	    const events = await ask('events.poll', { cursor: started.cursor ?? 0 });
54	    const done = (events.events ?? []).find(e => e.type === 'walk' && e.data.task_id === accepted.task_id);
55	    if (done) return done.data;
56	    if (Date.now() > deadline) return { status: 'timeout', task_id: accepted.task_id };
57	  }
58	}
59	
60	export const mcbuddy = {
61	  status: () => ask('status'),
62	  find: args => ask('world.find', args),
63	  column: args => ask('world.column', args),
64	  digest: args => ask('world.digest', args),
65	  standFor: cell => ask('agent.stand_for', cell),
66	  pick: cell => ask('agent.pick', cell),
67	  dig: cell => ask('agent.break', cell),
68	  place: cell => ask('agent.place', cell),
69	  say: text => ask('agent.say', { text }),
70	  tp: (x, y, z) => ask('agent.teleport', { x, y, z }),   // rig operation, needs dev_writes
71	  walkTo,
72	  // Walk to the nearest cell from which `cell` can actually be reached, then run the action.
73	  // This is the seam where a plan would otherwise burn turns discovering within_reach:false.
74	  async at(cell, action) {
75	    const stand = await this.standFor(cell);
76	    if (!stand.reachable) return { ok: false, reason: `no standing position in range: ${stand.reason ?? ''}` };
77	    const walked = await walkTo(parseCell(stand.stand));
78	    if (walked.status !== 'reached' && walked.status !== 'reached_near') {
79	      return { ok: false, reason: `could not get into range: ${walked.status}`, walked, stand: parseCell(stand.stand) };
80	    }
81	    const result = await this[action](cell);
82	    return { ok: true, walked, stand: parseCell(stand.stand), result };
83	  },
84	};
85	
86	/**
87	 * Run one program. Resolves with the program's own return value — that value is the only thing that
88	 * should ever re-enter a model's context, which is the whole point of PTC.
89	 *
90	 * `log` streams progress out of the runner as it happens; a plan that runs for minutes and prints
91	 * nothing looks exactly like a hang, which is worse than slow.
92	 */

2	name: feedback-commit-hygiene
3	description: On "注意gitignore" / commit requests: audit the exact staged set, exclude generated intermediates, scan for secrets, and report what was deliberately kept vs dropped.
4	metadata:
5	  type: feedback
6	---
7	
8	The user asks for commits with an explicit nod to ignore rules ("注意gitignore"). Treat that as a checklist, not a formality:
9	
10	- Preview the staged set first (`git add -An --dry-run`), group it by directory, and look for anything unexpected before staging.
11	- **Exclude generated intermediates even when they look like source.** `icons/source.png` was a 1024×1024 PNG written by `scripts/make-icon.cjs`; its *outputs* (`src-tauri/icons/`, referenced by `tauri.conf.json`) are committed, so the intermediate was ignored instead.
12	- **Keep deliberately-tracked generated files, and say why**: `src/lib/bindings/*.ts` (ts-rs output the frontend imports directly) and both lockfiles.
13	- Scan for secrets and credential-shaped files across the staged list, and report the largest blobs.
14	- After committing, verify the ignored directories are genuinely absent from the tree rather than trusting `.gitignore`.
15	
16	**Why:** this project accumulates output in several places that are easy to commit by accident, and one was found during the first-ever commit: a duplicate `src-tauri/bindings/` produced because `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` run from the repo root **skips `src-tauri/.cargo/config.toml`**, so `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` goes unset and ts-rs falls back to `<manifest>/bindings`. The repo had zero commits, so a bad initial commit would have been permanent.
17	
18	**How to apply:** on any commit request, run the audit, delete or gitignore stray generated output, then report the outcome as: files committed, what was excluded and why, and what was kept despite being generated. Never push unless asked. Run `cargo test` from inside `src-tauri/`, not from the repo root, to avoid regenerating the stray bindings dir.
19	
20	- **Report local state that never enters the repo separately.** Gitignored dev fixtures (`run/config/mcbuddy.properties` flags, blocks written into a scratch world) are invisible to `git status`, so say what was changed there rather than letting a clean tree imply nothing was touched.
21	
22	**Commit a safety point as soon as something is verified — don't bundle to the end.** Asked "现在提交 还是 等验收过了再提", he chose commit-now, three times in one long debug session. **Why:** the work is a sequence of live-measured fixes against a game process that can be restarted or crash at any moment; an uncommitted verified fix is the one loss he won't recover. **How to apply:** when a change is measured working, stage exactly those files, audit the list, and commit before starting the next hypothesis. Message bodies that carry the evidence — measurements, `file:line` citations, and the mistakes made and reverted — drew no pushback at any length; he reads them as the record, so do not trim them to one line.
23	
24	Related: [[feedback-verify-before-claiming]], [[gitui-status-and-debts]], [[project-mcbuddy-workflow]], [[feedback-not-the-test-harness]].

93	export async function runProgram(source, { onLog = () => {}, timeoutMs = PLAN_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {
94	  // A plan may be written as `export default async (m) => ...` for the editor's sake; the vm has no
95	  // module system, so the wrapper is stripped and the expression is what runs. Not anchored, because
96	  // a plan normally opens with comments explaining itself.
97	  const body = source.replace(/export\s+default\s+/, '').trim();
98	  const context = vm.createContext({ mcbuddy, log: onLog });
99	  const startedAt = Date.now();
100	  let timer;
101	  try {
102	    const factory = await vm.runInContext(`(${body})`, context, { timeout: timeoutMs });
103	    // The timer must be cleared, not just raced against: an uncancelled 180s handle keeps the event
104	    // loop alive after the answer is already printed, so a caller waiting on this process hangs for
105	    // the full deadline after every successful run.
106	    const result = await Promise.race([
107	      factory(mcbuddy),
108	      new Promise((_, reject) => {
109	        timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('plan deadline exceeded')), timeoutMs);
110	      }),
111	    ]);
112	    return { ok: true, ms: Date.now() - startedAt, result };
113	  } catch (err) {
114	    return { ok: false, ms: Date.now() - startedAt, error: String(err?.message ?? err) };
115	  } finally {
116	    clearTimeout(timer);
117	  }
118	}

#### Thinking

Multiplayer factory default: `chat-spam-threshold-seconds = 10`. So vanilla MP allows a burst of 10 messages then needs 1s of cool-down per message beyond that (each message costs 20 ticks, budget = 200 ticks = 10s, decaying 1/tick).

Effective semantics with TickThrottler(20, 200): count += 20 per message, -1 per tick. Under threshold while count < 200. So you can send 9 immediately (count 180 < 200 ok); the 10th pushes count to 200 → not under threshold → disconnect (in MP, for non-op non-owner). Steady state: 1 message/second.

Now: our integrated server has threshold=0 → guard disabled. So for a background companion I implement the same *shape* (a TickThrottler-style counter) but our own numbers, and I should reuse vanilla's class rather than invent a limiter: `net.minecraft.util.TickThrottler` is public and instantiable! `new TickThrottler(20, 20*10)` gives exactly the MP-default behavior. That's the "reuse vanilla's predicate instead of writing a new formula" pattern already ratified in this repo (M3 stand-position reused vanilla's reach predicate). Good consistency, minimal code.

Design decisions:
1. Where: in `BuddyAgent.say`, before broadcasting. Static field `chatSpamThrottler`.
2. Decay: TickThrottler must be ticked once per server tick to decay. Who ticks it? There's probably an existing tick hook (M0.5 tick source / a mixin on ServerLevel.tick or MinecraftServer.tick). Need to find where our mod ticks per-tick logic. Let me grep for `tick()` in BuddyAgent/Mixin.
3. Behaviour on over-limit: **do NOT disconnect** (we're not vanilla's network layer; and disconnecting the fake player kills the agent — that's catastrophic and wrong). Instead: refuse the message and return `{said:false, reason:"rate_limited", retry_after_ticks:N}`. The tool result stays informative so the model can decide.

(first.retry_after_ticks ?? 20) * 50 + 300 : 0,\n      said_after_wait: after_wait ? after_wait.said : 'never hit the wall',\n    },\n    null,\n    1,\n  ),\n);\n",

317	         return;
318	      }

Design: 
```js
import { statSync } from 'node:fs';
// The version the host reports is stamped from the files we were loaded from, because a long-lived
// shell keeps serving the module it read at spawn: when a tool face says `m.events is not a function`
// the question is whether the code is wrong or the process is stale, and that is not otherwise
// observable from inside the session.
const STAMP = ['mcp.mjs', 'ptc-host.mjs'].map(f => statSync(new URL(f, import.meta.url)).mtimeMs).join('.');
const SERVER_INFO = { name: 'mcbuddy', version: `0.0.1+${STAMP}` };
```
mtimeMs is a float like 1762200000000.123 — join gives long string. Use Math.round → seconds? Readable enough: `0.0.1+<epochsec>.<epochsec>`. Also log it at `listening` so mcp.log shows which build each spawn was.

async (m) => {
  const X0=-175, X1=-171, Z0=81, Z1=85, CX=-173, CZ=83;
  const inside = await m.walkTo({x:CX, y:86, z:CZ});
  let picked = await m.pick({x:CX, y:85, z:CZ});
  const cells=[];
  for (let y=86;y<=88;y++) for(let x=X0;x<=X1;x++) for(let z=Z0;z<=Z1;z++){
    const ring = x===X0||x===X1||z===Z0||z===Z1;
    if(!ring) continue;
    if(x===CX && z===Z1 && (y===86||y===87)) continue; // door
    cells.push({x,y,z});
  }
  for(let z=Z1;z>=Z0;z--) for(let x=X0;x<=X1;x++) cells.push({x,y:89,z}); // roof
  let ok=0, fails=[], walks=0;
  for(const c of cells){
    let st=await m.status();
    const heldNow = st.agent.hotbar[st.agent.selected_slot];
    if(!heldNow || !heldNow.startsWith('stone')){ picked = await m.pick({x:CX,y:85,z:CZ}); }
    let r = await m.place(c);
    if(!r.placed){ const a=await m.at(c,'place'); walks++; if(a.ok && a.result && a.result.placed) r=a.result; else r=a.result||a; }
    if(r && r.placed) ok++; else fails.push({cell:c.x+','+c.y+','+c.z, reason:r&&r.reason||('still '+ (r&&r.target_after))});
  }
  return {inside: inside.status, total: cells.length, placed: ok, failed: fails, extra_walks: walks, pos_after: (await m.status()).agent.pos};
}

  "content": "// 5×5 石屋：墙 3 高（y86-88）、平顶（y89）、门留 1×2 在 +z 面。全部走 agent.place（原版裁决），零直接写方块。\n// 跑法：node scripts/ptc.mjs scratch/house.mjs   或作为 mcbuddy_run_program 的 source 原样贴进去。\n// 顺序要点：屋顶按 z 从外 inward 逐行放，保证每一格都有已放置的相邻面可点；门只空 y86/87，y88 必须闭合，\n// 否则屋顶第一行失去支撑（place 找不到 support 会回 no solid neighbour to click from）。\nasync (m) => {\n  const X0 = -175, X1 = -171, Z0 = 81, Z1 = 85, CX = -173, CZ = 83;\n  const inside = await m.walkTo({ x: CX, y: 86, z: CZ });\n  await m.pick({ x: CX, y: 85, z: CZ });\n\n  const cells = [];\n  for (let y = 86; y <= 88; y++) {\n    for (let x = X0; x <= X1; x++) {\n      for (let z = Z0; z <= Z1; z++) {\n        const ring = x === X0 || x === X1 || z === Z0 || z === Z1;\n        if (!ring) continue;\n        if (x === CX && z === Z1 && (y === 86 || y === 87)) continue;\n        cells.push({ x, y, z });\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  for (let z = Z1; z >= Z0; z--) {\n    for (let x = X0; x <= X1; x++) cells.push({ x, y: 89, z });\n  }\n\n  let ok = 0, picks = 1, walks = 0;\n  const fails = [];\n  for (const c of cells) {\n    const st = await m.status();\n    const heldNow = st.agent.hotbar[st.agent.selected_slot] || '';\n    // 创造模式下这道保险不会触发（放置不消耗），进生存就是必需品。别把它当冗余删掉。\n    if (!heldNow.startsWith('stone')) { await m.pick({ x: CX, y: 85, z: CZ }); picks++; }\n    let r = await m.place(c);\n    if (!r.placed) {\n      const a = await m.at(c, 'place');\n      walks++;\n      r = a && a.result ? a.result : a;\n    }\n    if (r && r.placed) ok++;\n    else fails.push({ cell: `${c.x},${c.y},${c.z}`, why: (r && (r.reason || r.target_after)) || 'unknown' });\n  }\n\n  const s = await m.status();\n  return {\n    got_inside: inside.status,\n    planned: cells.length,\n    placed: ok,\n    picks,\n    fallback_walks: walks,\n    failures: fails.slice(0, 8),\n    pos: s.agent.pos,\n    held: s.agent.hotbar[s.agent.selected_slot],\n  };\n}\n",
  "file_path": "D:\\mcbuddy-mod\\scratch\\house.mjs"
}
```

{
  "content": "// 5×5 石屋：墙 3 高（y86-88）、平顶（y89）、门留 1×2 在 +z 面。全部走 agent.place（原版裁决），零直接写方块。\n// 跑法：node scripts/ptc.mjs scratch/house.mjs   或作为 mcbuddy_run_program 的 source 原样贴进去。\n// 顺序要点：屋顶按 z 从外 inward 逐行放，保证每一格都有已放置的相邻面可点；门只空 y86/87，y88 必须闭合，\n// 否则屋顶第一行失去支撑（place 找不到 support 会回 no solid neighbour to click from）。\nasync (m) => {\n  const X0 = -175, X1 = -171, Z0 = 81, Z1 = 85, CX = -173, CZ = 83;\n  const inside = await m.walkTo({ x: CX, y: 86, z: CZ });\n  await m.pick({ x: CX, y: 85, z: CZ });\n\n  const cells = [];\n  for (let y = 86; y <= 88; y++) {\n    for (let x = X0; x <= X1; x++) {\n      for (let z = Z0; z <= Z1; z++) {\n        const ring = x === X0 || x === X1 || z === Z0 || z === Z1;\n        if (!ring) continue;\n        if (x === CX && z === Z1 && (y === 86 || y === 87)) continue;\n        cells.push({ x, y, z });\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  for (let z = Z1; z >= Z0; z--) {\n    for (let x = X0; x <= X1; x++) cells.push({ x, y: 89, z });\n  }\n\n  let ok = 0, picks = 1, walks = 0;\n  const fails = [];\n  for (const c of cells) {\n    const st = await m.status();\n    const heldNow = st.agent.hotbar[st.agent.selected_slot] || '';\n    // 创造模式下这道保险不会触发（放置不消耗），进生存就是必需品。别把它当冗余删掉。\n    if (!heldNow.startsWith('stone')) { await m.pick({ x: CX, y: 85, z: CZ }); picks++; }\n    let r = await m.place(c);\n    if (!r.placed) {\n      const a = await m.at(c, 'place');\n      walks++;\n      r = a && a.result ? a.result : a;\n    }\n    if (r && r.placed) ok++;\n    else fails.push({ cell: `${c.x},${c.y},${c.z}`, why: (r && (r.reason || r.target_after)) || 'unknown' });\n  }\n\n  const s = await m.status();\n  return {\n    got_inside: inside.status,\n    planned: cells.length,\n    placed: ok,\n    picks,\n    fallback_walks: walks,\n    failures: fails.slice(0, 8),\n    pos: s.agent.pos,\n    held: s.agent.hotbar[s.agent.selected_slot],\n  };\n}\n",
  "file_path": "D:\\mcbuddy-mod\\scratch\\house.mjs"
}

The question: "在 llm 的视角，这些房子是以什么数据结构输出的？" — i.e., what is the representation of the house from the model's point of view? The answer: the house is NOT a data structure at all in the model's context — it's:
1. **Input side (what the model wrote)**: a JS program (text) whose geometry is *implicit* in loops — the model emitted ~40 lines of code with X0/X1/Z0/Z1 and the ring test; the 71 cells were expanded by the host, not by the model. Only the program's *return value* re-enters context: `{planned:71, placed:71, failures:[], ...}`.
2. **Output side (what came back)**: a compact summary object — counts + a bounded failure list (`.slice(0,8)`) + position. Not a block list.
3. **Verification**: a second program returning `{verified_stone:71, mismatch_total:0}` — again scalars.
4. **The world itself is the data structure** — the house lives in the save, not in context. Perception of it is *query-shaped*: `m.column` per column returns `["86 block.minecraft.stone", ...]` strings; `m.digest` returns aggregated `[id, count]` pairs; `m.find` returns `{matches:[{x,y,z,dist}], total_matches}`.

So the honest answer with the token economics: the model never held a 71-element block list in context; it held a program + 3 small objects. That's the whole point of PTC (as ratified).

I should also point out the *loss* this creates, since he's asking as a designer: because the model only sees scalars, it cannot "see" the house; it can only re-query. If we want it to reason about the shape later ("开门加窗"), it must re-derive geometry from a query (or from the saved program in scratch/house.mjs). That's the design tension: geometry lives in code + world, not in context. And the mcp-app UI idea is exactly the missing piece for *human* viewing (he just took a screenshot manually — which per memory is a missing-probe signal! He screenshotted to check the build → that means we lack an observation surface for him... Actually it means he wanted to see it. Also worth noting the measurement: how many tokens did the house cost me? The build call returned ~250 bytes; the verification ~300 bytes; the program text I wrote ~1.2KB. Total context for a 71-block build ≈ under 2KB. Contrast: if the house were represented as a block list (71 × ~20 chars = 1.4KB just for coordinates, and it'd scale with size, not with *decisions*).

Key insight to state: **the unit of output is a decision, not a block**. Cost scales with the description length (5×5, h3, door), not with volume.

#### Thinking

He says: do the blueprint first. Also notes: later the LLM could use screenshots for aesthetic verification; and MC has rich commands which could be wrapped as tool calls, or we could prepare an external specialized agent loop for the game. Those are later. "你先推进我们需要推进的" — proceed with what needs doing now = **蓝图 (blueprint)**.

So: design + implement blueprint storage.

What is a blueprint, minimally useful?
Goal: make "what did I change" queryable data, so the model can remember, modify, and precisely undo — without re-reading the world.

Design space:
A. **Change log (diff) at the bridge**: every `agent.place` / `agent.break` already knows target cell + before/after id. Record them into a ring/list keyed by a "task" or "op id". Then `world.diff(from_seq,to_seq)` or `blueprint.list()`.
B. **Explicit blueprint objects**: `blueprint.save(name, cells)` / `blueprint.load(name)` — model declares a named structure; the program records cells as it builds.
C. **Auto-grouped**: the bridge accumulates edits since a marker and can emit them as a compact structure with bounds/summary.

The most valuable and least speculative: **A + a thin naming layer**. Because:
- The record already exists in `place` (`target_before`, `target_after`) — we just throw it away.
- It gives undo for free (reverse the list).
- It's honest: it's what actually happened, not what we intended (crucial: my build reported placed:71 but the *world* is the truth; a log of actual transitions is verifiable).
- Naming: `blueprint.mark()` starts a named batch; `blueprint.close()` returns summary. Or simpler: every write op carries an optional `bp` tag from the program.

Minimal design I'd implement:
1. Java: an `EditLog` (ring buffer, like EventQueue) recording `{seq, tick, op:place|break|pad, x,y,z, before, after, bp?}`. Only records **actual transitions** (after != before).
2. Bridge methods:
   - `world.edits` params `{since:seq, bp?:name, limit?}` → returns compact list + latest cursor + bounds (min/max xyz, count, distinct blocks).
   - `agent.undo` params `{bp?:name, since?:seq}` → reverse the recorded transitions **through the same vanilla-judgement path** (place for a block that appeared, break/dig for one that vanished). This is the risky one — needs care (M3 rules: never setBlock). Undo of a *break* (restoring a block) requires placing the original block id — but the agent may not hold that block, and creative `pick` can obtain it from... the block is gone. Hmm. That's a real constraint: you cannot restore an arbitrary destroyed block through the player path without the item. So undo works for **placements** (dig them out) but not reliably for **destructions** (needs the item; in creative you can't pick a block that no longer exists).
   
   → So scope undo to placements only, and say so. That's honest and still 90% of what he wants ("精确拆掉").
3. PTC surface: `m.edits({since, bp})`, `m.mark(name)`? Simpler: pass the blueprint name on the write call itself: `m.place(cell, 'house')`. Hmm — `agent.place` params already have x/y/z; add optional `bp`. And `m.undo({bp})`.
4. Shell: no new tool (writes only through run_program, per the ratified rule). Reads: is `world.edits` worth a 7th tool? The rule says write ops go through run_program; reads got their own tools. But "工具少而粗是预算" — I'd NOT add a 7th tool; the model can query edits via run_program (`m.edits(...)`). Keep the tool surface at 6. Good, consistent with the recorded decision.

Also `pad` (dev fixture) writes blocks via setBlock? WorldFixture — it's dev-only; should it be logged? It's a rig op; log it too but tagged `pad` so undo can be told to ignore it... Simpler: log only agent.place/agent.break (the player-identity path). Keep minimal.

Wait — is `break` implemented as a real mining sequence? M3: break via synthesized inbound packets (start digging → finish). It records the block gone + drops. So `after` = air.

7	/** Bounded, cursor-addressed event log so the protocol stays stateless: callers pass the last cursor back. */
8	public final class EventQueue {
9	   private static final int CAPACITY = 256;
10	   private static final ArrayDeque<Entry> ENTRIES = new ArrayDeque<>();
11	   private static long sequence;
12	
13	   private record Entry(long seq, String type, JsonObject data) {
14	   }

16	   public static synchronized void add(final String type, final JsonObject data) {
17	      ENTRIES.addLast(new Entry(++sequence, type, data));
18	      while (ENTRIES.size() > CAPACITY) {
19	         ENTRIES.removeFirst();
20	      }
21	   }

23	   public static synchronized JsonObject poll(final long cursor) {
24	      JsonArray events = new JsonArray();
25	      long newest = cursor;
26	      for (Entry entry : ENTRIES) {
27	         if (entry.seq() > cursor) {
28	            JsonObject wrapper = new JsonObject();
29	            wrapper.addProperty("seq", entry.seq());
30	            wrapper.addProperty("type", entry.type());
31	            wrapper.add("data", entry.data());
32	            events.add(wrapper);

35	      }
36	      JsonObject result = new JsonObject();
37	      result.addProperty("cursor", newest);
38	      result.add("events", events);
39	      long dropped = sequence - (ENTRIES.isEmpty() ? 0 : ENTRIES.peekFirst().seq());
40	      if (dropped > 0) {
41	         result.addProperty("older_than_cursor_dropped", (int)dropped);
42	      }
43	      return result;
44	   }
45	
46	   public static synchronized long latest() {
47	      return sequence;
48	   }

Both methods have exact success points with `before`/`after` known:

```js
async (m) => {
  const s = await m.status();
  const bx = Math.floor(s.agent.pos.x), bz = Math.floor(s.agent.pos.z);
  const by = Math.floor(s.agent.pos.y);   // feet level
  // a 2x2 patio two blocks in front, at feet level, on the pad
  const cells = [[bx+2,bz],[bx+3,bz],[bx+2,bz+1],[bx+3,bz+1]].map(([x,z]) => ({x, y: by, z, bp:'patio'}));
  await m.pick({x:bx, y:by-1, z:bz});  // floor stone under feet
  const placed = [];
  for (const c of cells) { const r = await m.at(c, 'place'); placed.push(!!(r && r.ok) ? (r.result && r.result.placed) : false); }
  const log = await m.edits({ bp:'patio' });
  const dug = [];
  for (const e of log.edits.slice().reverse()) { if (e.op === 'place') { const r = await m.at({x:e.x,y:e.y,z:e.z}, 'dig'); dug.push(!!(r && r.ok && r.result && r.result.broken)); } }
  const after = await m.edits({ bp:'patio' });
  const truth = [];
  for (const e of log.edits) { const col = await m.column({x:e.x, z:e.z, y0:e.y, y1:e.y}); truth.push(col.column[0]); }
  return { cells: cells.map(c=>c.x+','+c.y+','+c.z), placed, log_after_build: {matching: log.matching, returned: log.returned, bounds: log.bounds, kinds: log.placed_kinds, first: log.edits[0]}, dug, cells_now: truth };
}
```

That's a real bug in `at()`: it should skip the walk when the agent is already within reach of the target (or already at the stand cell). And more generally: `at()` walks before acting even when the action is already in reach — wasting time and hitting this bug.

The fix: in `at()`, first try the action directly; if it fails with an in-range indication... hmm, better: use `standFor`'s answer — if the agent's current position is already within reach of the target, act directly. How to know "within reach"? `place`/`dig` results carry `within_reach` — so: try the action; if `within_reach` is true and it succeeded, done. Actually simplest robust ordering:

```js
async at(cell, action) {
  // Try from where it stands first: walking when already in range wastes a round trip and, measured
  // 2026-10-04, the pathfinder answers "no route" for a goal the agent is already standing in.
  const direct = await this[action](cell);
  if (direct && (direct.placed || direct.broken || direct.held !== undefined ...)) 
```
Hmm, success shape differs per action ('place'→placed, 'dig'→broken, 'pick'→held/changed). Cleaner: check `within_reach` true AND success flag; else fall back to stand+walk+retry.

Define: `const done = r => r && (r.placed || r.broken || r.changed || (r.held && r.held.length>0 && r.within_reach))` — getting fiddly.

Simplest correct: 
```js
async at(cell, action) {
  const first = await this[action](cell);
  if (first && first.within_reach && succeeded(action, first)) return {ok:true, direct:true, result:first};
  if (first && first.within_reach && !succeeded(...)) return {ok:false, reason:'in range but refused', result:first}; // no point walking
  ... else stand+walk+retry
}
```
where `succeeded(action, r)` = action==='place' ? r.placed : action==='dig' ? r.broken : action==='pick' ? (r.held||'').length>0 : true.

Key insight worth encoding: **`within_reach:false` means "move closer"; `within_reach:true` + failure means "moving won't help"** — that's a genuinely better failure taxonomy and prevents the useless walk entirely.

Where's the right layer? Java WalkTask: if goal == current block → immediately `reached`. That's the honest fix (it's the pathfinder's contract). But it costs another restart to verify.

**顺手挖到一个真 bug**（第一次撤销全 `broken:false`）：`m.at()` 原先无条件**先走路再动手**，而它当时**已经站在目标格上** —— `WalkTask:82` 把"路径只有一个节点（就是脚下）"当成"寻路没找到路"，两种相反的答案共用一个字符串。修法两层：`at()` 改成**先伸手再挪窝**，拿 `within_reach` 当判别器（false 才值得走过去；true 却失败 → `in range but refused`，走过去没用）。**改完 5/5 成功**。Java 侧的 `already_at_target` 拆分已编译，**待下次重启一起验**（不单独花你一次重启）。另外记一条：`Vec3` 在 26.3 **没有** `blockPosition()`，得写 `BlockPos.containing(vec)` —— 我按 1.x 记忆写就被编译器当场拒了。

**蓝图的天花板，需要你定一件事**：`EditLog` 是**内存态**，重启即失忆。它能答"我这轮盖了什么"，不能答"这个存档里我盖过什么"。两条路代价不同：
- **持久化**（`run/mcbuddy-blueprints.json`）→ 能跨会话想起，但要处理"世界被别人改过"导致蓝图与现实不符；
- **把蓝图当成程序**（`scratch/house.mjs` 那类）→ 天然可重放、可改参数重建，但它记的是"意图"不是"事实"。
我倾向**两个都要但分工不同**：事实日志持久化（可撤销/可审计），程序留作可重放的图纸。你点头我就按这个做。

你提的两条我归好位了，按你说的先不做：截图验美观我认为**站得住**，因为它低频、事后、由人挑时机 —— 探针管"对不对"，截图管"好不好看"，不冲突（原版有现成 F2 路径，要处理的是写盘位置和给模型前的压缩）。而 MC 的 `/setblock /fill /give` 那批**不能**直接封成 tool（M3 黑名单：绕过玩家身份），但 `/locate /time /weather` 这类不写世界的查询封起来很便宜；外置 agent loop 其实已经有了 —— `run_program` 就是它的宿主，缺的只是长计划的进度通知。

**需要你一次点击**：`m.edits` 在 agent 面还没有（刚实测 `m.edits is not a function`，因为你上次重启是 13:5x，而 `ptc-host.mjs` 是 14:3x 改的 —— 构建戳现在能直接告诉我们差在哪）。面板里再 disable/enable 一次即可。

This\nadds the missing structure -- an ordered log of the transitions the agent caused.\n\nRecorded at the two places where the world is known to have changed (placeAt's\nplaced, breakAt's after != before), not where a plan asked for a cell. The\ndistinction is the reason for the log: a placement that silently no-oped because of\nreach or a missing support face must never be remembered as built, or the blueprint\ndrifts from the world and the model reasons about a building that is not there.\n\nNamed as it happens: place/dig/pick accept an optional `bp` string, so a program\ntags its own work and later reads it back with world.edits {bp}. {
  "content": "// 蓝图往返：命名建一组格子 -> 按名字读回 -> 照着日志拆掉 -> 读世界确认真的没了。\n// 跑法：node scripts/ptc.mjs scratch/blueprint.mjs\nasync (m) => {\n  const s = await m.status();\n  const bx = Math.floor(s.agent.pos.x), by = Math.floor(s.agent.pos.y), bz = Math.floor(s.agent.pos.z);\n  await m.pick({ x: bx, y: by - 1, z: bz });   // 脚下那一格石台，拿材料\n\n  const cells = [\n    [bx + 2, bz], [bx + 3, bz], [bx + 2, bz + 1], [bx + 3, bz + 1],\n  ].map(([x, z]) => ({ x, y: by, z, bp: 'patio' }));\n\n  const built = [];\n  for (const c of cells) {\n    const r = await m.at(c, 'place');\n    built.push({ at: c.x + ',' + c.y + ',' + c.z, placed: !!(r && r.ok && r.result && r.result.placed) });\n  }\n\n  const log = await m.edits({ bp: 'patio' });\n\n  const dug = [];\n  for (const e of log.edits.slice().reverse()) {\n    if (e.op !== 'place') continue;\n    const r = await m.at({ x: e.x, y: e.y, z: e.z }, 'dig');\n    dug.push({ at: e.x + ',' + e.y + ',' + e.z, broken: !!(r && r.ok && r.result && r.result.broken) });\n  }\n\n  const truth = [];\n  for (const e of log.edits) {\n    const col = await m.column({ x: e.x, z: e.z, y0: e.y, y1: e.y });\n    truth.push(e.x + ',' + e.y + ',' + e.z + ' = ' + (col.column || ['?'])[0]);\n  }\n\n  const after = await m.edits({ bp: 'patio' });\n  return {\n    built,\n    log_at_build: { matching: log.matching, bounds: log.bounds, kinds: log.placed_kinds, first: log.edits[0] },\n    dug,\n    cells_now: truth,\n    log_after_undo: { matching: after.matching, places: after.edits.filter(e => e.op === 'place').length, breaks: after.edits.filter(e => e.op === 'break').length },\n  };\n}\n",
  "file_path": "D:\\mcbuddy-mod\\scratch\\blueprint.mjs"
}

#### Thinking

Critical finding, and it's a blocker worth surfacing immediately:

> "当前原生沙箱只支持 Linux；其他平台会明确关闭 MCP，不会无沙箱启动。"

He's on **Windows** (win32). So bugent's MCP is **explicitly disabled on non-Linux platforms** unless something overrides. That means: configuring mcbuddy in bugent's `[[mcp.servers]]` will do nothing on Windows unless (a) he runs bugent under WSL/Linux, or (b) there's an override flag.

Let me verify that claim in code rather than trusting the comment — grep for the platform check in src/mcp/runtime.ts or stdio.ts (e.g., `platform !== 'linux'`).

Also `read/write/exec` are **sandbox path/exec allowances**, not tool classification (per the schema comments: "Additional external write paths", "Additional executable roots"). So they're about what the child process may touch — meaning for mcbuddy, the child needs to reach 127.0.0.1:25731 → `network = "none"` default would **block the loopback bridge**! That's a second real integration issue: mcbuddy's shell talks to the game over TCP loopback; the default MCP sandbox policy is `network = "none"`. So he'd need `network = "allowlist"` + `network_allow` entries, or "all".

That's a genuinely useful, concrete finding: two blockers (Linux-only sandbox on Windows; default no-network vs our loopback bridge), plus the fix shape. Let me verify both in code quickly.

#### Thinking

Decisive: on Windows, MCP servers **do spawn**, just unsandboxed (`spawnUnsandboxed`), with env whitelist still applied. So the comment in his config.toml ("其他平台会明确关闭 MCP") is **stale/wrong** relative to the code — the code explicitly spawns unsandboxed and notes "缺的只是内核隔离，逐次授权的门控不变".

That's a valuable finding for him (a doc/code mismatch in his own project — and he has a bug-hunting agent, so he'll appreciate it).

And since the sandbox isn't applied on Windows, `network = "none"` **is not enforced there either** — so the loopback bridge works on Windows today. On Linux it WOULD be blocked unless `network_allow` includes 127.0.0.1 (or network="all"). That's the precise, platform-dependent answer.

So integration recipe:
```toml
[[mcp.servers]]
id = "mcbuddy"
cmd = ["node", "D:/mcbuddy-mod/scripts/mcp.mjs"]
# Windows: 无原生沙箱，network 不生效；Linux 要放行回环
# network = "allowlist"

不需要 `cwd`：外壳的日志是绝对路径、`ptc-host.mjs` 按自身路径解析、桥接写死 `127.0.0.1:25731`（这条 HANDOFF 里早就记过"子进程 cwd 不在仓库"）。`MCBUDDY_PORT` 这些都有默认值，`env` 可以留空。

**2. 你 config.toml 第 92 行那条注释是错的**（我没改，等你决定）：

**3. 真正需要注意的是 `network`，而且是分平台的**：我们的外壳靠 TCP 回环连桥接，而 MCP server 默认 `network = "none"`。Windows 上沙箱整条路径不生效，所以今天直接能用；**一旦你切到 Linux，默认策略会把回环掐掉**，那时必须写 `network = "allowlist"` + `network_allow = ["127.0.0.1:25731"]`。这个坑现在不炸，换平台才炸，值得先记下来。

## 快速开始

```bash
# 安装当前 checkout 的 Bugent Bun fork 到 runtime/bun/
bun run runtime:install

# 可选：备份现有 ~/.bun/bin/bun 后替换为 fork
bun run runtime:install -- --global

bun install

# 无需网络与密钥，验证链路
bun run src/index.ts --mock -p "你好"

# 接真实模型（配置在 ~/.bugent/config.toml，首次运行自动生成）
bun run src/index.ts -p "写个 hello world"

# 交互式（自动进入 TUI，需要 TTY）
bun run src/index.ts

# 纯文本 REPL（不走 TUI）
bun run src/index.ts --plain

# 权限与沙箱
bun run src/index.ts --mode read-only         # 读免问；写工作区/写外部/联网逐次批准
bun run src/index.ts --mode workspace-write   # 读+写工作区免问；写外部/联网逐次批准（默认）
bun run src/index.ts --mode no-sandbox        # 全部免问（沙箱仍在，只是不拦截）
bun run src/index.ts --yes                    # 跳过所有规则检查（危险）

# 会话
bun run src/index.ts --sessions       # 列出已保存的会话
bun run src/index.ts --resume <id>    # 恢复会话继续聊
bun run src/index.ts --no-persist     # 不落盘

# 测试与类型检查
bun test
bun run typecheck

### **Assistant**

这个问题的答案取决于一个可测的事实：你的客户端有没有声明 `sampling`（服务端反向请求模型）或 `elicitation`。它握手时已经把 capabilities 发进 `mcp.log` 了 —— 去读，别猜。



`ping` 那 4 次命中是我自测脚本发的 `method=ping`。但要先确认日志有没有把 `params` 截断，否则"没看到 sampling"就是假证据。



**MCP 有反向唤醒机制，但你的客户端没声明。** Qoder 桌面端在 `initialize` 里给的 capabilities **只有 `extensions`** —— 我核对了 `mcp.mjs:144` 那个 300 字符截断点，capabilities 对象在可见文本里是完整闭合的（`{"capabilities":{"extensions":{…}},"clientInfo":…}`），所以"没看到 `sampling`"不是漏看，是**真没有**。这意味着按协议我不能假定它能被 server 反向唤起。

协议侧那三个东西分别是：`sampling/createMessage`（server 请求 client 跑模型）、`elicitation/create`（server 请求用户输入）、`notifications/*`（log / resources updated / tools list_changed）。stdio 本身是全双工，所以**技术上我们随时能发** `sampling/createMessage` —— 只是对面没人接。

**所以我不建议再设计一套 stdio。** 缺的不是协议，是"**谁拥有循环、什么时候醒**"。三条落地路径按代价排：

1. **bugent 侧加 watchdog（推荐）**。你已经有的比你想的多：`--resume <id>`、会话持久化、`maxSteps` 默认 800。写个 ~40 行宿主：长轮询 `mcbuddy_events`，攒到一条 `chat`（或 `wedged`）就把文本当 user turn 注入一次 `bugent --resume <session> -p "…"`，跑完把结果 `agent.say` 回游戏。**协议一行都不新增**，只是给现有循环装了个触发器 —— 而且方向是对的：喊话的人是玩家，不是模型。
2. **Qoder 侧今天就能试，零代码**：这个环境里就有 `qoder_cron` + `send_message_to_chat_session`，定时唤醒一个会话去 poll events。缺点是它是**拉**（间隔=延迟），而且绑死 Qoder。
3. **mod 侧主动推**：把 bridge 从请求-响应扩成长连接 NDJSON 事件流，外围订阅。它彻底解决 idle，但等于自己实现一遍 sampling —— 只有当 bugent 是唯一宿主时才划算。

**不管选哪条，有一个决策必须先定：唤醒判据。** 现在普通聊天**全部进事件环**，`!buddy` 开头的反而在 HEAD 被吃掉。如果"任何聊天都唤醒模型"，一个多人世界或一群僵尸就能把你的 token 预算烧光。所以我建议唤醒词做成**服务端过滤**（配置项 `wake_prefix`，默认 `@buddy` 之类），并且**复用今天刚立起来的那个形状**：`say` 是出站节流，`wake` 需要入站节流 —— 两者同属"原版守卫管不到"的那一类（假玩家既不能签名，也不被 `detectChatRateSpam` 约束，单人里那个守卫压根不存在）。

**一个连带的硬前置**：自动唤醒 + `--mode workspace-write` 就等于"没人看着也能改世界"，这正好撞上我上一条说的**桥接默认开、无鉴权**。所以路径 1 上线前，得先给 bridge 加一个共享口令（或默认关、显式开）。这两件事是绑在一起的，别先做唤醒再做鉴权。

要我把路径 1 的接口面先设计出来（事件→turn 的注入格式、唤醒过滤器、以及 bugent 那侧需要暴露什么），还是你更想先把鉴权那块补上？

# mcbuddy × bugent 游戏 agent 接入计划
> scope statement, 更新时间 2026-10-04, 分支 master

## 0. 一句话结论
不 fork。mcbuddy 负责"任何 MCP 客户端都能玩"，bugent 只是第一个外部宿主。

## 1. 分工边界（为什么这样切）
- mcbuddy 侧：协议 + mod 能力 + 与游戏无关的唤醒语义
- bugent 侧：模型循环 + 会话/记忆/权限
- 依据：游戏特化没有一样东西在 loop 里（systemPromptFile schema.ts:18、[[mcp.servers]] toml.ts:290、MemoryRepo/sessions）；fork 的代价是双向 merge 一份活跃 loop。

## 2. 已核实的 bugent 事实（接入前要知道的）
| 事实 | 出处 | 影响 |
- MCP 客户端已有（stdio）src/mcp/{manager,runtime,stdio,tools}.ts；工具名 mcp__<id>__<tool>
- 配置键 id|name / cmd[] / cwd / env / env_values / read/write/exec / network / network_allow / state_dir / limits — config/toml.ts:290-330
- 原生沙箱只支持 linux（stdio.ts:30-32），但**非 linux 是显式 spawnUnsandboxed**（stdio.ts:266-271），不是"关闭 MCP"。→ docs 注释/配置模板里那句"其他平台会明确关闭 MCP"与代码不符，待修（我标 BUG 候选）
- MCP server 默认 network=none → Linux 上会掐掉 127.0.0.1:25731，需要 network_allow
- webui/headless bridge **不装 MCP**（entry-webui.ts 顶部注释），CLI/TUI 装 → 最小闭环走 CLI
- 流式已有：core/loop 的 LoopHooks、protocol/types.ts 的 UiEnvelope/UiEventType/TurnSendPayload → 左下角回显是订阅者，不是新架构

## 3. mcbuddy 侧要做的（优先级即施工顺序）
P0 桥接鉴权 bridge_token（env 可传，任何客户端都能配）
P0 产品验收标准（M5/M6 判据）—— 现在"完善"没有定义
P1 **client-agnostic 的唤醒**：`m.wait_for({match, timeout_ticks})` 在 run_program 里阻塞等事件 → 把"拉"变成"请求内的推"。理由：Qoder 桌面端 initialize 只声明 extensions（实测 mcp.log，capabilities 对象完整闭合），没有 sampling；不能把唤醒寄托在客户端实现 sampling 上。这条对**任何** MCP 客户端都成立，代价是占住一个请求（需要 progress 或分段兜底）。
P1 notifications/progress（支持它的客户端体验好；不支持的退回 P1 的 wait_for）
P2 ui.actionbar {to,text} 发给**真实玩家**连接（ClientboundSetActionBarTextPacket 在 26.3 确认存在）；发给假玩家=黑洞
P2 蓝图持久化（EditLog 现在内存态）
P2 mcp-app UI 资源（客户端已声明 io.modelcontextprotocol/ui）
P3 生存模式里程碑

## 4. 唤醒语义（已定）
- 触发：`@buddy` 前缀，任意真实玩家（按 UUID 排除 agent，**不能按人名** —— 今天量到 Player814→Player921→Player271）
- 入站节流（与出站 say 限流同形，因为单人里原版 detectChatRateSpam 压根不存在：IntegratedServer:212 → 阈值 0 → TickThrottler:24 永久放行）
- 合并窗口 1.5s；跑中排队 1；再多的丢弃但 say 一句"我在忙"
- `!buddy` 仍是命令通道（HEAD 吃掉、不进环），`@buddy` 必须进环 —— 两条并存要在 HANDOFF 写清
- 自激安全：self_echo_in_ring:0 已实测

## 5. 分阶段
阶段 A（mcbuddy 独立可做，不碰 bugent）：token + wait_for + 验收标准 + 测试骨架
阶段 B（第一次真闭环）：scripts/watch.mjs 订阅桥接事件 → spawn `bun run src/index.ts --resume <id> -p`（走 CLI，因为它装了 MCP）→ agent.say 回话。bugent 侧只加一份 bugent.game.toml。
阶段 C（要流式回显时）：bugent 的 headless bridge 接上 MCP 装配；watch.mjs 从 CLI 换成 WS 订阅；MC 侧加 ui.actionbar。

## 6. 不做/已否决
- fork bugent（理由见 1）
- 自动切"游戏模式"（判据本身是模型在做的事，最难 debug；手动选 config+session 成本相同）
- 把 /setblock /fill 之类封成 tool（M3 黑名单：绕过玩家身份）
- 依赖 sampling 唤醒（客户端没声明）

## 7. 交接面
mcbuddy 的跨会话接口是 D:\mcbuddy-mod\docs\HANDOFF.md；本文只写 bugent 侧要知道的。

Since the bridge is connection-per-request (ptc-host `ask()` opens a new socket for every call!), a per-connection auth is as expensive as per-request.

Check: `ask()` in ptc-host opens `net.connect` per call. So per-connection auth = per-call token anyway. Simplest and least churn: **token on every request** as a top-level field `token`, checked in BridgeHandlers/BridgeServer before dispatch. Then ptc-host's `ask()` adds it automatically from env `MCBUDDY_TOKEN`, and the shell inherits env. And probe.mjs too.

Design decision: top-level `token` field on the request envelope; server compares with configured token using constant-time compare; mismatch → error response `{ok:false, error:"unauthorized"}` and **don't echo the token**. Also log a warning at most once per minute to avoid log spam? Keep simple: log the rejection without the token.

#### Thinking

Two important discoveries while reading:

1. **`MAX_PER_TICK = 4`** — only 4 requests are executed per server tick. At 20 tps that's 80 req/s ceiling; fine for us. But it also means a *queued* request waits for a free slot. Relevant for `wait_for`: **I must NOT implement wait_by blocking on the server thread** — it would stall the whole bridge queue and the tick. So `wait_for` must be implemented on the *host* (JS) side: poll `events.poll` until match or timeout. That's the honest design: "push-within-one-request" from the client's point of view, polling inside the host process. Good — and it means no Java change for #2 at all. Nice.

2. **`await()` has a 5000ms deadline** on the accept thread — a request that doesn't get answered within 5s returns "game did not answer within 5s". Note `pending.wait(200)` inside `synchronized(pending)` — fine.

Also note: the accept thread's response for an unauthorized request can be produced **without** queueing to the server thread — better (cheaper, and rejects before touching the game). So the auth check belongs in `serve()` (accept thread), not in BridgeHandlers. That's the right choke point: one place, covers every method, no server-thread cost.

Now: where to compare? `BuddyConfig.bridgeToken`. Constant-time compare: `MessageDigest.isEqual(a, b)` is the standard constant-time compare in the JDK — use that (no crypto dependency).

Design:
- Request envelope: top-level `"token"` string.
- If `BuddyConfig.bridgeToken` is empty → accept everything (dev default, documented).
- If set → require `token` equal; `ping` exempt (liveness only, so a client can produce a good error message: "bridge up, unauthorized").
- Reject with `BridgeJson.error(id, "unauthorized: bridge requires a token (config bridge_token)")` — must not echo the supplied token.
- Log: warn at most once per connection? A flood of bad tokens shouldn't spam the log. Keep: log once per minute using a timestamp guard. Hmm, complexity. Simpler: log at debug/warn only when the *first* rejection on that connection happens — since serve() loops per line on a connection, I can track a boolean per connection. That's 2 lines and gives one log line per attacking connection. Good.

Now #2: `m.wait_for` in ptc-host.mjs — pure JS, polls events until match or deadline.

Design:
```js
/**
 * Wait inside one request instead of making the model poll: pull becomes push-within-a-call, which
 * works for every MCP client -- none of them were measured to implement `sampling`, so a wake path
 * built on reverse requests would break the day someone uses another client.
 *
 * It polls from the host because the bridge executes at most MAX_PER_TICK requests per server tick:
 * a blocking wait on the Java side would hold the queue and the tick itself.
 */
export async function waitFor({ match, cursor = 0, timeoutMs = 60000, pollMs = 400 } = {}) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let at = cursor;
  for (;;) {
    const page = await ask('events.poll', { cursor: at });
    const hits = (page.events ?? []).filter(e => !match || e.type === match.type || (match.text && String(e.data?.text ?? '').includes(match.text)));
```
Hmm, the match spec. Keep it simple and honest:
- `match`: string type name (`'chat'`, `'walk'`) or an object `{type, text}` where text is a substring of `data.text`.

Return: `{ matched: event|null, cursor, waited_ms, timed_out: bool }`.

Careful: `events.poll` with cursor returns events *after* cursor and the newest cursor. If I filter and none match, continue with the new cursor.

Also must respect the plan deadline: the caller's `runProgram` races with timeoutMs=180s; a wait_for with 60s default is fine.

Let me write it:

```js
export async function waitFor(opts = {}) {
  const { match = null, cursor = 0, timeout_ms = 60000, poll_ms = 400 } = opts;
  const wantsType = typeof match === 'string' ? match : match?.type ?? null;
  const wantsText = typeof match === 'object' && match ? match.text ?? null : null;
  const deadline = Date.now() + Math.min(timeout_ms, PLAN_TIMEOUT_MS);
  let at = cursor;
  const started = Date.now();
  let seen = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const page = await ask('events.poll', { cursor: at });
    const events = page.events ?? [];
    seen += events.length;
    for (const e of events) {
      at = Math.max(at, e.seq);
      if (wantsType && e.type !== wantsType) continue;
      if (wantsText && !String(e.data?.text ?? '').includes(wantsText)) continue;
      return { matched: e, cursor: page.cursor, waited_ms: Date.now() - started, seen };
    }
    at = Math.max(at, page.cursor ?? at);
    if (Date.now() >= deadline) return { matched: null, cursor: at, waited_ms: Date.now() - started, seen, timed_out: true };
    await sleep(poll_ms);
  }
}
```
Note `sleep` is defined at line ~37 (const sleep = ...). waitFor must be after it. And `page.cursor` semantics: poll returns `cursor` = newest seq seen.

Careful: the `for` loop updates `at` per event; but if events is empty and page.cursor advanced (dropped older), fine.
